subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a `gateway.peers`-based cross-gateway session-tool route now, or keep session tools gateway-local until the broader federation trust model is defined?
rationale: The requested workflow is real, but this PR expands gateway trust, message delivery, session state, and config surfaces; automation cannot choose the permanent security/product boundary safely.

options.title: Design the core contract first
options.body: Define peer identity, URL allowlisting, token handling, replay/idempotency, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing core cross-gateway session routing.

options.title: Route through plugin/MCP seams
options.body: Keep core session tools gateway-local and expose only missing extension seams needed for an external bridge implementation.

options.title: Pause for the federation FRD
options.body: Wait for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 to settle the bridge protocol and identity model before accepting this implementation shape.

recommendation.title: Design the core contract first
recommendation.body: Define peer identity, URL allowlisting, token handling, replay/idempotency, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing core cross-gateway session routing.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner candidate is already identified in the canonical issue as the strongest routing point for the session-tool, gateway config, and security-boundary decision.
